project.title: Adaptive Transport Protocol for Real-Time Streaming over UDP
project.claim: Adaptive transmission will provide better and more stable streaming performance than fixed-rate UDP under varying conditions.
project.summary: A reliable streaming protocol built directly on UDP sockets. The sender adapts its transmission rate to measured loss, RTT and jitter, and a custom emulator recreates poor network conditions so adaptive and fixed-rate sending can be compared with repeatable experiments.
highlights: Custom AUDP packet format with sequence numbers and SHA-256 checksums
Acknowledgements, timeout-based retransmission and RTT/RTO estimation
Network emulator for packet loss, delay and jitter, seeded for repeatability
Adaptive rate control compared against a fixed-rate baseline
End-to-end stream reconstruction verified by SHA-256 hash
Responsive dashboard and local test server for running and presenting the experiments

members.name: Nishtha Bhushan
contributions: Designed the AUDP v1 packet format: magic bytes, version, type, sequence number, nanosecond timestamp, payload length
Implemented SHA-256 checksum validation with a constant-time comparison and strict malformed-packet rejection
Built the UDP sender: chunking, sequence numbering, pacing and the END packet carrying the packet count
Built the UDP receiver: out-of-order reassembly, duplicate detection, missing-packet reporting and post-END wait
Wrote the packet and transfer test suites, including SHA-256 end-to-end integrity checks
Maintains the repository, README and project documentation

members.name: Prakhar Manish Srivastava
contributions: Added the ACK packet type and ACK validation rules
Implemented the RTT estimator (RFC 6298 smoothing, Karn's algorithm, exponential back-off)
Implemented the Stop-and-Wait ARQ controller with timeouts and a retry limit
Integrated ARQ into the sender and receiver, including the acknowledged END handshake and receiver linger
Wrote the ARQ transfer and reliability tests (lost data, lost ACK, duplicates, retry exhaustion)
